project.name: my-browser-qute
project.description: my-browser-qute — daily-driver browser built from the qutebrowser source VENDORED in src/browser/ (flat snapshot of upstream v3.7.0, no patch series). Fully rebranded: binary my-browser-qute, config dir ~/.config/my-browser-qute, desktop id org.mybrowser.qute, mybrowser:// URL scheme (registered alongside qute://, which still works). Daemon-side integrations: FIDO2 passkeys via da_fido2-vault-broker, password autofill via da_autofill-rbw-rofi. Dir is db_my-browser-qute.

browser._default_browser_note: true → home-module sets xdg.mimeApps so my-browser-qute owns http(s)/html/about/unknown scheme handlers (the system default browser). Flip to false to disown. Data-driven toggle read by src/nix/home-module.nix.
browser.comment: The browser is OUR source now (src/browser/), not a nixpkgs package + patches. Config is rendered to config.py by src/nix/home-module.nix, which owns the JSON→Python projection itself (home-manager's programs.qutebrowser hard-codes ~/.config/qutebrowser and is no longer used).

data_sources.comment: All four JSON files are read by the home-manager module at evaluation time and rendered into my-browser-qute's config.py. Edit JSON, rebuild home-manager, browser picks up the new state.

release.comment: Standalone my-browser-qute config bundle (config.py + quickmarks + bookmarks/urls + qute-bookmarks.html + --basedir launcher), independent of the ~6GB 37-module desktop home-manager closure. Built by `build.sh release` (nix build .#standalone), published to BOTH a GitHub Release (rolling tag, --clobber) and GHCR (oras, matching the repo's all-services-as-GHCR-images pattern) via `build.sh gh-release`/`build.sh ghcr-push`. install-standalone / the desktop flake pull from the GitHub Release ONLY — GHCR is a redundant/discoverable mirror, not a consumption path.

fork.comment: The my-browser-qute binary packaged as a PORTABLE self-extracting executable via `nix bundle .#my-browser-qute` (~640MB, QtWebEngine included, under GitHub's 2GB asset limit). Built by `build.sh fork-release`, published to its own rolling GitHub Release tag by `build.sh fork-gh-release`. A single-file download that runs the browser without Nix. gzip'd for transfer.

fido2_vault_broker.comment: WebAuthn over /dev/hidraw — my-browser-qute/Chromium auto-discovers the virtual FIDO2 device when the daemon is running. No extra config needed.

autofill_rbw_rofi.comment: Password autofill via global hotkey is OS-level (handled by da_autofill-rbw-rofi). my-browser-qute sees the typed keystrokes like any other window.

vaultwarden_bitwarden_cli.comment: In-page autofill (Ctrl-Shift-B) via the in-tree qute-bitwarden userscript (src/browser/misc/userscripts/qute-bitwarden — vendored with the rest of the source). Uses the official `bw` CLI against our self-hosted Vaultwarden server (API-compatible with real Bitwarden). Matches by the vault item's saved URL (bw list items --url <domain>) — no need to rename entries. Session persisted via keyctl (keyutils), auto-locks after runtime.auto_lock_seconds. home.packages gets bitwarden-cli + keyutils; a home.activation step idempotently runs `bw config server <server_url>` (no secrets — the interactive `bw login` step is a ONE-TIME manual step, cannot be automated declaratively since it requires the master password).
